THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Spot-the-missing-item is memory made visible: hold the first panel in your head, scan the copy, and name the gap. The blue toy car’s empty dashed outline gives a strong hint for beginners — cover the left panel for the expert version.

  • Visual memory
  • Comparing two panels
  • Naming missing items
  • Careful scanning
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Say the rule first

    Every puzzle has a rule — a pattern, a size order, two clues together. Say it aloud before solving, and the sheet solves itself.

  2. Point before circling

    Have your child point at the answer and say why, then circle it. The pointing keeps the thinking honest.

  3. Check together with the answer line

    The grown-up answer strip at the bottom lets you check without guessing — and lets your child play teacher.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Sort real things too

After the sorting sheets, sort socks or spoons the same way. Real objects make the rule permanent.

Patterns everywhere

Lay out apple-grape-apple snacks and ask what comes next. The sheet teaches the skill; the kitchen keeps it.

Mazes build pencil control too

The maze sheet doubles as pencil practice — slow and steady on the path matters more than speed.

Answer guide

The blue toy car is missing (its dashed empty spot shows where it sat).

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

It belongs to Logic, Thinking & Problem-Solving (Class 30) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole logic collection lives at /worksheets/logic/. Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
